sources.articleTitle: Nigeria’s external debt up 6.6% to $145bn in 2025 – World Bank

headline: World Bank Reports Nigeria External Debt Rose To 145 Billion Dollars
seoTitle: Nigeria External Debt Hits 145 Billion Dollars
metaDescription: The World Bank reports that Nigeria's external debt has grown to 145 billion dollars in 2025, marking a 6.6 percent increase from the previous year.
aiSummaryBullets: The World Bank data shows Nigeria's total external debt reached 145.015 billion dollars in 2025.
This figure represents a 6.6 percent annual increase compared to the previous reporting period.
Total external debt has increased by 74.3 percent over the last decade, rising from 83.21 billion dollars in 2015.
aiContextParagraph: According to the latest figures released by the World Bank, Nigeria has experienced a significant rise in its external debt obligations over the past ten years. The report indicates that the country's debt stock grew from 83.21 billion dollars in 2015 to 145.015 billion dollars by 2025. This escalation reflects a total increase of 74.3 percent within the decade. For the most recent year, the data highlights a 6.6 percent rise in external debt levels. These findings are based on official debt statistics monitored by the World Bank, which track international borrowing trends across developing economies. The accumulation of this debt remains a central point of analysis for economic observers assessing the nation's fiscal health and long-term borrowing capacity in the current international financial climate.
